label: Tiny radioactive source
summary: Ionisation smoke alarms hold a tiny americium-241 source inside a small metal chamber. Sealed in its housing it is harmless; opening, scraping, eating or breathing it in is the problem. Radioactive sources from hospitals, labs, factories and industrial gauges are far stronger and can kill: leave them alone.
signs: Smoke alarm labelled ionisation, with a radiation symbol or the words Americium 241
A small metal can or cage on the alarm's circuit board
Old glow-in-the-dark watch and instrument dials, mostly from before about 1970, may use radium paint

Heavy lead or steel containers, capsules, pellets or machine heads marked with the radiation symbol, from hospitals, labs, factories, oil wells or road-building density gauges: these are deadly, not tiny
do: Take the battery out and leave the alarm in one piece. Don't open it for the buzzer or the chamber: Kidde's guide says never to take one apart
To get rid of an old alarm, take the battery out and dispose of the whole alarm: the CNSC accepts household garbage (not recycling or compost) or return to the maker
Wash hands after handling a broken or damaged alarm

Strong sources (gauges, capsules, shielded containers): if you can't avoid being near one, keep the time short, the distance long and concrete or lead between you and it. The CNSC sets a 2 m perimeter round a damaged portable gauge
dont: Don't open the alarm, and don't crush, scrape or heat it or its chamber
Don't keep piles of them where people sleep or eat
Don't scrape or sand old luminous paint
Don't let children play with them
Don't touch, open, cut or carry off anything like that: get away, keep everyone out, and mark the spot
ppe: Gloves if a chamber is damaged
firstAid: Touched a damaged source: wash hands well with soap and water
If someone swallowed a source or breathed dust from one, get medical advice; the risk is small but real
Nausea, vomiting, or burns and blisters that appeared without a fire after handling a metal object: suspect radiation; get away from the object, wash, and get medical help
